treatment_X and treatment_Y are one subject's paired binary outcomes (McNemar test), repeated measures as columns beside a one-row-per-subject id.
N1Spikes, N2Spikes and N3Spikes are three neurons' spike counts over the same Orientation rows, each neuron's repeated measures stored as a column.
Q1 to Q11 are one respondent's binary item scores (Cronbach's alpha, wide by name), the respondent's repeated item responses as columns.
tip ~ total_bill and party attributes, one row per bill; day and time are few-level predictors, no column indexes a unit the bills repeat within.
income ~ sex + race + age + hs_week, a census logistic-regression example, one row per person and no cluster column.
vote ~ age * party_id, a logistic-regression example, one row per respondent; party_id is a three-level predictor, not a unit.
count over one hourly series (instant a row id, dteday, hour and weekday time stamps), no replicated unit; one time series, so no grouping factor.
id indexes UK firms with one row per year each (Arellano-Bond employment panel, c1 labels firm-year); the documented xtabond fit has no random effect but rows repeat within id.
company (label Company) indexes firms with one row per time each, the Grunfeld investment panel; its rows are company 1 onward of grunfeld.dta, so it re-files as a subset of that table.
id (label Group (country)) and country index countries with one row per year each, a balanced panel of real exchange rates fitted by xtunitroot.
idcode (label Municipality ID) indexes Swedish municipalities with one row per year 1979-1987 each, a fiscal panel fitted by dynamic GMM or panel VAR.
farm and school are individual binary attributes; household variables (value, rent, ftotinc) repeat but no household or cluster id column exists to index them.
